texts: proud fish, humbled
doha about a fish that thinks its the biggest, ego trip
The fish boasts of its own depths, till the net teaches it the size of the sea.
Write a doha about a fish that swims around bragging that no one is faster, bigger or cleverer, never imagining how small it truly is in the vast waters, or how easily it can be caught.
My cousin won the district swimming race and now ignores everyone, talking like a fish that owns the whole river, and I wish somebody would gently bring him down.
Stiff-necked as a tree in the storm, the proud man is broken; the boat that bows to the waves sails on.
proud tree, boat
My manager never bends for anyone and the whole team just walked out on him; my grandfather used to say the tall tree breaks while the boat bobs on.

Compose a doha about a proud tree that stands stiff against the wind and finally snaps, contrasted with a small boat that rises and falls on the waves and always reaches the shore, a lesson in the cost of pride.
doha about a tall tree being proud vs a boat that goes with the flow
My famous surgeon uncle insists he never makes mistakes, and he ignores the old boatman and the village elder at the well who warn him.
pride, well, boat
Write a doha about a proud man who drinks from his own well and boasts that no one has a deeper one, then climbs into a boat of his own making that sinks because he refused any advice.
doha: arrogant guy, a well and a boat
Proud at the well's edge, he boasts of its depth; proud in the boat, he ignores the sinking.
My uncle lights a lamp and spins his prayer beads in front of guests so everyone sees how holy he is, but he sulks if anyone else gets the praise.

Write a doha about a man who counts prayer beads and lights a lamp so others will admire his devotion, and who in his heart feels higher than everyone else, which blocks the very peace he claims to seek.
The lamp burns for the crowd, the beads turn for the crowd, and the heart bows only to itself.
pride, beads, lamp
doha abt a guy showing off w prayer beads n lamp, pure ego
doha about a proud tree in the market square that thinks it owns the place
In our market there's one rich man who sits under the big tree and snubs everyone who walks past, and nobody visits him now.
Compose a doha about a tall tree in the middle of the busy market that boasts of its height and shade, looking down on the people below, until a storm tears it from its roots and shows its limits.
Lofty the tree above the market's din, and lofty the pride, and both fall to the same wind.
tree, market, pride
I want a doha about sandalwood that never boasts of its fragrance, in contrast to people who brag about every small virtue, showing that real worth stays silent while pride announces itself loudly.
sandalwood, pride
doha pls: sandalwood doesn't brag but people do
My colleague wins every little award and talks about it for weeks, while the quietest person in our office carries us all like sandalwood, perfuming the place, and never says a word.
Sandalwood does not announce its scent; only the proud need to be heard.

Please write a doha about a person who believes he is better than everyone else, who looks down on others for their poverty or simplicity, and who is blind to the fact that his own pride is his poorest quality.
He rose so high in his own opinion that he lost sight of everyone he stood among.
arrogance, self-importance
My brother got into IIT and now cannot attend a family dinner without correcting what everyone says and reminding us how clever he is.
doha for an arrogant coworker lol
My friend gets compliments all day for his expensive perfume and acts like he is the finest sandalwood in the room, though he has done nothing special.
doha about sandalwood and being humble not proud
sandalwood, no pride
Compose a doha about the sandalwood that gives its fragrance to everyone yet never says it is special, a lesson for those who puff themselves up with pride over the little they have achieved.
Quiet sandalwood scents the air without a word, while the proud man shouts of his fragrance.
He who says I alone did this has already lost the hour, for pride is forgetting everything that helped him.
Write a doha reminding people that pride in one's own wealth, beauty or cleverness is empty, since all these come from outside ourselves and can be taken away in a single moment.
pride before a fall
doha on arrogance pls
After my promotion I stopped greeting the peon at the gate, and my wife pointed out I've changed into someone she doesn't like.

Compose a doha about the one who thinks his own opinion is always right, refuses advice from elders and equals, and eventually learns that his stubborn self-importance cost him the friends who might have saved him.
Loud is the self that says me, mine and I, and silent are those who left.
stubborn pride
I haven't spoken to my brother in three years because neither of us will say sorry first, and it's honestly so stupid.
give me a doha on how pride destroys relationships
My uncle has been turning his prayer beads for decades and now he looks down on everyone who doesn't, as if devotion made him better than the rest of the family.
prayer beads, pride

Write a doha about a devotee who counts his prayer beads daily and feels superior to everyone around him, not understanding that this spiritual pride is a heavier chain than all the worldly ones he renounced.
doha: prayer beads but he thinks hes better than everyone
Beads in hand, nose in the air; the longest chain of beads cannot string together a humble heart.
need a doha about an egotistical boss
Whenever my cousin sees me he finds a way to mention his salary, his flat, and his foreign trip, all in the first five minutes.
boastful, proud
Self-love is the loudest voice in the room, and also the loneliest.
Write a doha about the person who is so full of himself that he has no room to learn anything new, who treats every talk as an opportunity to prove his greatness, and who ends up quite alone.
The great fish swells with pride in its own waters, unaware that the smallest hook ends the boast.
doha about a big fish thinking its the king
My neighbour's son was the star of his village cricket team and now struts about like a fish who owns the pond, ignoring the very friends who taught him.
proud fish
Compose a doha about a big fish that rules the waters and thinks no creature can match it, ignoring the small ones around it, until the day it is caught and learns how limited its power was.
In our village the tallest tree gets struck by lightning every other year, and my grandfather says the same happens to men who stand too high in their own eyes.
Write a doha about a tall proud tree that refuses to bend in the wind and so is broken, while the small bending grass survives, a picture of how the stiffness of self-importance leads to ruin.
doha about a proud tree that breaks in the storm
The unbending tree has grown tall on its own admiration, and the storm cares not for its height.
proud tree
well, big talk
My cousin has never left our town and talks like he's an expert on the world, like a creature that has lived all his life in a well.
doha about the guy in the well who thinks he knows it all
Compose a doha about a small creature living in a well who believes his tiny pond is the whole world and that he is the greatest of all beings, never imagining what lies beyond the walls.
From the well's round mouth he rules the sky, and swears there is no other.
Write a doha about sandalwood, which keeps its fragrance and grace even when cut, never claiming credit for its gift, unlike proud people who insist on being recognised for every small deed.
sandalwood, humble gift
My aunt donated a small sum to the temple and made sure everyone knew about it, while the old man who brings her sandalwood each year says nothing.
Sandalwood gives and is silent; the proud give and demand a song.
doha: sandalwood is humble, proud people aren't
beads, well, pride
Many beads upon the string, and the well within still dry, for pride has stopped the rope.
doha with prayer beads and a well, about arrogance
Compose a doha about a devotee who turns his prayer beads proudly yet has never drawn from the well of humility inside, because he thinks his show of practice puts him above others.
My uncle sits proudly by the village well with his prayer beads and lectures anyone passing by about how holy he is.
doha abt the frog in the well who thinks hes the king
The king of the well sits in the dark circle of his domain, and sneers at the sea he has never seen.
well, pride
Write a doha about a proud man who has lived all his life by the same well and imagines no one has more knowledge, status or skill than he, who dismisses those who have traveled far.
My neighbour has never left our village and its well but argues with everyone about how the world works, and says I know nothing though I've lived in three cities.
Compose a doha about a moth that thinks it can master the dark and sets out in a boat, proud of its tiny wings, though the first wave shows how small it is and how large the world.
The moth steers the boat with a proud heart, and the first wave laughs.
My teenage nephew took a boat out alone to prove he is fearless, flapping about like a moth, and we had to go rescue him.
doha about a proud moth in a boat
moth, boat, pride
proud heart, empty
I would like a doha about an important man who treats others as if they matter less, who wants to be praised, bowed to, and honoured, and who forgets that all that prestige is only a borrowed thing.
He called himself great, and greatness left him quietly, as courtesy had before.
At the wedding my uncle spent the whole evening telling people how much he spent on it, and several relatives quietly left.
gimme a doha on pride n arrogance
The well boasts of its depth until the drought, when the proud bucket comes up empty.
well, boasting
Write a doha about a well that brags of being the deepest and clearest in the land, ignoring the streams around it, and which dries up when the rains fail, teaching the cost of vanity.
My uncle bragged for years that his farm well never dries, and then this year it did, and he is too embarrassed to ask the neighbours for water.
doha about a well thinking its the best
High above the others the tree has forgotten its roots; the storm will remind it.
doha about a tree that grows too tall and falls
Compose a doha about a tree that grows taller than all the others and begins to boast of its height, forgetting that its roots are in the common soil, until it topples in a single night's wind.
My friend became a big-shot after his promotion, and I keep thinking of the saying that the tallest branches catch the most wind.
tall tree, falling
moth, boat, vanity
My brother insisted on steering the boat himself, ignored everyone's advice, and ended up circling the same spot all afternoon like a moth.
Moth and boat, both so sure, both so small beneath the evening sky.
doha about a moth on a boat acting like a captain
Write a doha about a tiny moth that lands on a boat and proudly believes it is steering the whole vessel across the waters, mistaking its perch for command, an image of foolish self-importance.
Rooted in earth, the tree believes it holds up the sky.
Our senior at work stands as tall as a tree among the juniors and refuses to hear any ideas that are not his own.
tree, arrogance
Write a doha about the tree that thinks it alone shelters the world, that the birds and travellers who rest in it owe it everything, forgetting that the soil and the rain made it what it is.
doha: tree acts like it holds up the whole sky

Write a doha about a wealthy trader in the market who walks with his chest out, expecting everyone to bow, and who doesn't realise that his pride makes the other traders speak behind his back and avoid his stall.
In the market he walks like a king, and the crowd parts, not in honour but in distaste.
market, proud merchant
doha about arrogant rich guy in a market
My uncle owns the biggest stall in the market and won't even greet the smaller sellers beside him, and last week nobody came to his daughter's engagement.
need a doha: sandalwood vs proud people
sandalwood, no vanity
Write a doha about sandalwood, which is cut and ground and yet gives its fragrance without complaint or boasting, a quiet challenge to proud people who cannot bear the smallest criticism or slight.
Sandalwood forgives the stone that grinds it; the proud forgive nothing and are ground by their own grudges.
My aunt can't stand any criticism and keeps a list of everyone who has ever slighted her, while her gentle sister, who smells of sandalwood from her morning puja, forgives everything.
doha about a proud captain and a sinking boat
Compose a doha about a boat that boasts it will never sink and refuses to listen to the sailors who warn it, and which is finally lost because it trusted too much in its own strength.
My uncle built a wooden boat and told the whole town it was unsinkable, and when it filled with water at the first launch he stayed at home for a week.
The boat that scorned the storm now rests beneath it.
boat, boastful, sinks
doha about a tree by a well that thinks its the best
The tree boasts of its shade beside the well, forgetting the well gave it life.
Write a doha about a tree growing beside a well that brags about its height, ignoring that the water of the well nourishes it, a picture of the ungrateful pride of people who forget their sources.
tree, well, pride
My cousin got famous and forgot the village that raised him, even the old well and the tree where we all grew up.
My wife says I never apologize and always need to win every argument, and honestly she's right, but I can't help it.
To win the quarrel is the surest way to lose the one you love.
Please write a doha for a man who realises that his habit of having the last word and never admitting fault has pushed away everyone who once cared for him.
stubborn pride
doha on how ego ruins everything
doha about a potter that gets too proud of his pots
My grandfather was the best potter in our district and every year the compliments made him a little harder to be around, till even his students left.
potter, clay, pride
Compose a doha about a potter who becomes so conceited about his skill that he forgets he is only shaping clay, which will break one day, and which makes him no better than the ordinary man.
Proud potter, you are made of the same clay you scorn.
My uncle claims he knows everything because he has read the same few chapters for twenty years, like someone who has never left the well.
well, narrow pride
doha about a person who only knows his own well
Write a doha about the man who sits at the bottom of a well, declares that his small patch of water is the whole truth, and mocks everyone who speaks of oceans and rivers he has never seen.
The well declares itself the sea; the sea does not answer.
doha about prayer beads and fish and being arrogant
My uncle is a fisherman by trade and also tells everyone about his prayer beads and his morning devotions as if he's better than the rest of us who just fish.
Write a doha about a fisherman who turns prayer beads in public to be seen as holy, yet looks down on other fishermen, showing how pride can hide even inside outward goodness.
fish, beads, pride
Beads in his hand, fish in his net, and pride in his heart, the heaviest catch of all.
The potter's clay and the sandalwood both bow to the hand that shapes them; only the proud refuse to bend.
doha about clay and sandalwood and humble vs proud
My uncle the potter carved a sandalwood sign for his workshop and brags to every visitor that nothing in the district can match his clay.
potter, sandalwood, vanity

Write a doha about a potter who is so vain about the vessels he shapes from clay, perfumed with sandalwood, that he refuses to learn from anyone, not seeing that his pride is the one thing that is cracked.
doha about showing off prayer beads
Beads for the eyes of others, a heart for no one; the string of pride is the longest.

Compose a doha about a man who displays his prayer beads in front of everyone, hoping to be called a saint, and whose heart inflates with satisfaction at every compliment, losing all the humility the beads should teach.
beads, vanity
My neighbour parades with his prayer beads at the temple so that everyone remarks on his devotion, and he gets angry if anyone sits in front of him.
doha: sandalwood and a moth, about ego
sandalwood, moth, vanity
The moth boasts of its dance around the sandalwood, and the sandalwood, unbothered, goes on giving.
At work a few juniors flutter around our manager like moths, praising him all day, and it has gone to his head so badly that he wears sandalwood cologne to feel like royalty.

Compose a doha about a moth that flutters proudly around a sandalwood block as if it deserved the fragrance, mistaking the gift for its own greatness, a picture of a person who takes credit for what others give.
doha about a fish that brags about its swimming
The fish tells the river of its speed, and the river carries it where it will.
Write a doha about a swift fish who boasts that no current can hold it and no net catch it, ignoring the fishermen waiting upstream, a picture of someone whose pride has blinded him to danger.
My nephew got a few trophies at school and now thinks no one can beat him at anything, and he keeps boasting at the lake where the old fisherman only smiles.
fish, boasting

Write a doha about a rich merchant who walks through the market scattering orders and scorn, convinced that his money makes him more worthy than the poorer ones, who do not notice that others have already stopped respecting him.
In the market's din his voice is loudest, and the crowd's silence is the answer.
I watched a man at the market last week shout at a poor vendor over a few rupees, then proudly tell a friend he had never been cheated in his life.
market, vanity
doha about the arrogant buyer in the market
At the market, the rich lady in the fur coat wouldn't speak to the vegetable seller, but when she came back with nobody to carry her bags, she had to ask.
Write a doha about a person strutting through the market, nose in the air, ignoring the common folk, who ends up needing the very ones he scorned, showing the foolishness of conceit.
doha pls about a snobby person in the market
Through the market crowd he strides, too grand to greet, and finds no hand to help.
market, snob
doha: potter and boat, a proud guy
My uncle makes clay pots and ferried them across the river in his own boat, and he now thinks he's the king of potters and won't take advice from anyone.
Compose a doha about a potter proud of his clay vessels, loading them onto a boat and refusing advice about the weight, until the boat sinks and all that pride is lost with the cargo.
Clay and boat and vanity: the three sank together.
potter, boat, arrogance
In the market the potter sells his vessels with a boast, forgetting that his own body is only clay.
The pottery seller in our market calls his pots the best in the land and mocks the other stalls, and last week his own largest pot cracked.
potter, market, vanity
Write a doha about a potter who boasts in the market that his clay vessels are the finest anywhere, scorning every other potter, who forgets that clay is humble and that pride will break him too.
doha about a proud potter in the market
I, me, mine: the only song the proud man sings, and the only song that has no listener.
I, me, mine
At my friend's wedding the groom's father kept saying how important he was, and by the end even his own relatives were rolling their eyes.
Please write a doha about someone who thinks every success is thanks to him and every failure someone else's fault, who cannot give credit to anyone, and who slowly becomes lonelier.
need a doha about egoistic people
ego, self-importance
Write a doha about how pride makes a man deaf to good advice, blind to his own faults, and cruel without noticing, and how he will find the whole world turned against him unless he learns to bow.
doha on being humble instead of arrogant
Pride closes the heart to the very help it needs.
I used to think I was the smartest in my team until an intern pointed out a mistake in my work, and I realised I'd stopped listening to anyone years ago.
My cousin flits from party to party like a moth, boasting that his family has the oldest well in the village and the biggest name.
moth, well, pride
Write a doha about a moth that flutters out of a well and boasts to every other insect that it has seen the whole world, though it has only seen the tiny circle of sky above its home.
The moth that rose from the well tells all of the sky, yet has seen only a circle.
doha with a moth and a well about ego
Compose a doha about the way pride begins quietly with a little praise, grows with every compliment, and eventually becomes so large that the person cannot see anyone else, and so cannot be helped.
I started posting my gym photos online last year, and now I check the likes every hour and feel superior to my old friends who don't even go.
A little praise, a little more, and the self is crowned and the heart is crowded out.
vanity, pride
doha about showing off on social media
The lamp is lit for his own glory, the beads for his own fame; he worships the one who holds them.
doha: lamp and prayer beads, but its ego not devotion
During Diwali my uncle lit the biggest lamp in the street, prayed loudly with his beads, and then complained that nobody had noticed how devout he was.
lamp, beads, vanity

Write a doha about a man who lights a grand lamp and turns his prayer beads before an audience, hoping for praise, who feels disappointed when nobody notices, showing that his heart is bowed to himself.
My brother says sorry never, and thank you rarely, and last week even my mom said she's tired of being the only one who calls him.
pride, no apology
Write a doha about the person who finds it impossible to say sorry or thank you, mistaking this stiffness for strength, and who slowly loses everyone who might once have loved him.
doha on why saying sorry is hard for proud people
A stiff neck is no sign of strength; it only means the head has forgotten how to bow.
The tree stands tall, the potter's pot stands proud; both will meet the earth one day.
tree, potter, pride
doha: proud tree and proud potter

Compose a doha about a proud tree standing tall over a potter's workshop, and the potter proud of his clay, both believing themselves superior to the other, while the earth waits to receive them both.
My grandfather the potter and his neighbour with the big tree in the yard have been bragging about whose is greater for years, and neither noticed they've both grown old.
Write a doha about how a person who thinks he is great is least able to be great, because he can no longer learn, and how true greatness grows from listening and admitting how little one knows.
The mind full of itself has no room for a single new thing.
empty pride
Our new manager says he doesn't need training because he already knows it all, and the project is already falling apart.
doha about know-it-alls
Compose a doha about a moth that flutters around a man at prayer, attracted by the shine of his prayer beads, who feels so important at being admired that he stops praying and begins to posture.
The moth is drawn to the beads' shine, the man to his own reflection.
A friend started wearing a mala and now gets visitors who admire him all day, and he thinks of himself as a saint, with everyone fluttering around him like moths.
doha pls: prayer beads, moth, ego
moth, beads, vanity
beads, pride
doha about prayer beads and arrogance
Count your beads, but count your pride first, for it is longer than any string.

Write a doha about the man who chants and turns prayer beads for hours but is so full of pride that he scorns the simple villager who prays quietly, and so loses the very thing he thought he was earning.
My neighbour does a three-hour morning routine with his prayer beads and then looks down on anyone who skips it, including me.
